name: Pauillac

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Malbec sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
A ranking for Médoc châteaux left out of the 1855 classification. Any Médoc property may apply.

In 1855 brokers ranked Bordeaux estates by reputation and price. Reds were ranked from first to fifth growths, nearly all in the Médoc, and the sweet whites of Sauternes and Barsac from superior first growth to second growth.
keyfacts: It sits on the Left Bank of the Gironde within the Haut-Médoc, between St-Julien to the south and St-Estèphe to the north.
The vines grow on well-drained gravel terraces that run parallel to the Gironde estuary.
Cabernet Sauvignon dominates the blend, with Merlot for roundness and fruit and Cabernet Franc or, more rarely, Petit Verdot; Carmenère and Malbec are also allowed.

notes: Pauillac's main fruit flavor is usually blackcurrant, sometimes veering toward plum.
It is noted for a strong lead-pencil scent, and some wines show minty notes.
The wines are deeply colored, powerful and structured, and develop a highly complex bouquet with long aging.

blurb.text: A Haut-Médoc commune in Bordeaux for red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and other Bordeaux grapes. It has three of the five premier cru châteaux: Latour, Lafite Rothschild and Mouton Rothschild.
